beats: Big Bad Brain Wrestling: every move a lie, every bruise for real.
Action figure, four heads, one cardboard ring.

beats.text: The Babyface, high-flying moves; audiences cheer, a slave to approval.
The Heel, bear hugs and eye pokes; if they aren't booing, you aren't doing your job.
The Tweener, crowd split; you don't ask for it, so they want you more.
The Jobber, isolated and picked apart; you exist to make the other guy look good.
The Little Giant, tiny ant hoisting enormous elephant; defying the physics of size.
The Master Seller, reel back, limp to the ring, make them believe.
The Thigh Slap, a loud sound suggests high impact; an audio lie.
The Stomp Punch, kinetic misdirection.
The Oversell Clown, flying backwards from a gentle tap.
The No-Sell Monster, sit right back up; remove all tension for ego.
The Sacred Mask, the single biggest identifier; never remove it.
The Rudo Ripper, attempt to maim the mask; heat-generating garbage.
The Booker, spider in suit; the ending is pre-planned, you are just a puppet.
The Spot Caller, a basic outline, filled in with sweat.
The Cue Card Holder, short cuts for out-of-depth wrestlers.
The Hard Cam, if the camera didn't see it, it didn't happen.
The Empty Arena, pausing for a pop that never comes.
The Green Screen Crowd, chameleons pretending to be crowd; audio sweetening on a lie.
The Internet Smark, psychology without ever taking a bump.
The Real Injury, Goldberg's shoulder, the ring-post; the crowd goes nuts because it's real.
The Kayfabe Police, keep the secrets secret, or get fired.
The Finisher, the Leg Drop; if this hits, go home.
The False Finish, the art of the near-fall.
The Retirement Match, rising, and falling; see you next season.

beats: Click. Four heads, one body. Every bruise for real.
